# Assembled conversation management

`make linux-conversation-management-test` now uses the native assembled application in three fresh sessions: minimum 420×520, narrow 480×640 and wide 1060×780. Each compares 23 states and five images against unchanged v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. The [independent fixture](released-application-management.json), SHA-256 `88d572d87dd87eb8a6f2b573abaaba11be2f53b21d686d5688b67f0686dfd68c`, records actual GTK, store, clipboard and provider results. A focused replay is `bash linux/tests/run_application_smoke.sh management minimum`.

The external reference observer checks all 77 released modules against that commit before activation and checks imported paths/digests after shutdown. It drives the actual application, registered actions, buttons, menus, dialogs and private Escape input. No application handler, scheduler or service is replaced. The temporary collector stays under ignored `tmp/`; native Make uses only static observations and native external peers.

The existing application harness owns setup and acknowledged shutdown. Its real `ApplicationDesktop` callbacks connect the conversation workspace, review/capture controllers, History page and compatible stores. Two explicit input records have fixed identifiers/timestamps; only those seed fields use direct SQL before UI interaction. All resulting titles, originals, outputs, replies, grouping, prompt drafts, document text/carets, visible headings, dialog controls and clipboard bytes are observed. No generated result is injected or normalized away.

| Retired contract | Native observation and retained owner |
| --- | --- |
| Inline rename and current title refresh | Real title activation updates sidebar and History labels without losing edited source, prompt or the released caret/selection state |
| Empty title, Escape and stale rename | Invalid title remains editable; actual private Escape cancels; changing conversations prevents the old edit from renaming another record |
| Searchable merge and Cancel | Actual dialog begins disabled, search narrows to Roadmap, selection enables Merge, and Cancel preserves both records |
| Merge during active work | A real held Codex rewrite and a separate PCM capture each invalidate an already-open merge confirmation; cancellation then permits a positive merge |
| Edited source, originals, replies and draft migration | Positive merge preserves both immutable originals, combines edited source, migrates the processed replies and retains the unsent prompt |
| Incognito guards | Turning on the real setting invalidates a pending rename and deletion; stores remain unchanged |
| Recording guard and confirmed/cancelled cascade deletion | A real capture blocks deletion; after cancellation, Cancel preserves the merged conversation and Delete removes both records/replies and clears the editor/prompt |
| Delayed generated title versus human choice | Existing `title_jobs` owner retains actual provider scheduling and manual-title precedence; it is rerun without duplicating those cases here |
| Component geometry, atomic grouping and retained-file cleanup | Existing conversation, History and store owners retain their distinct contracts and are rerun where affected |

One explicit document rewrite starts a real native Codex protocol process and holds its response at the external endpoint; cancellation reaps it. Every size records that exact turn, including complete input/model/effort, and permits no extra management-triggered turn. The real speech HTTP peer receives zero requests. Recording guards use separate native PCM children rather than synthetic busy flags. Final shutdown requires all owned capture/provider processes and ephemeral provider workspaces to disappear. The private clipboard remains exactly `untouched management clipboard` throughout.

All fifteen images have zero differing pixels against the release, without masks: four complete X11 windows and one actual GSK popover texture per size. The views are inline title, sidebar menu, menu actions, selected merge dialog and empty state after deletion. Client allocations are 410×510, 470×630 and 1050×770; each popover texture is 179×192. Final reference logs are `tmp/native-management-final-source-{minimum,narrow,wide}.log`, with sessions `session.xCzWoT`, `session.T6Usoc` and `session.JaTh17` under the corresponding evidence directories. Native captures are `tmp/application/run.qC5PNi/{minimum,narrow,wide}/session.*/native-application-management/`; the exact metrics are in `tmp/native-management-final-reviewed-pixels.log`. Visual inspection also checked the minimum inline editor and merge dialog.

The former Make route fails at a positively verified interpreter trap in `tmp/native-management-before.log`. The final native target passes all three sessions with `/usr/bin/python3` and `uv` blocked and neither trap used (`tmp/native-management-final-make.log`, outer `tmp/native-management-final-make-evidence/session.a5T85A/`). The retired `conversation_management_smoke.py` had 218 lines and only its Make caller; shared rendering helpers retain their other consumers. Its former substituted services and synthetic activity flags are replaced by actual observable external operations.

The broader check passes fifteen application workflows/147 states plus the command/settings owner, 123 conversation states, fifteen History workflows/59 states and pending-response shutdown, and 28 title transactions/98 states plus owner exit. Evidence is `tmp/native-management-final-siblings.log`, root `tmp/application/run.rwn55r/session.ObUT9E/` and sibling `tmp/native-management-final-siblings-evidence/session.tOXZDz/`. Two initial broader runs exposed an existing three-second GTK focus-indicator timeout in the Live comparison. The [Live evidence](live-workspace-evidence.md) records its independent reference repair, four exact final images and a missing-input negative control; production focus behavior is unchanged.

Final actual `make test` passes 139 tests, zero failures and 68 ignored environment checks across 98 suites, both strict Clippy configurations, formatting and generated-document consistency. Relevant ignored desktop checks run explicitly above. Actual `make linux-python-test` passes 571 tests plus Ruff/formatting for 153 remaining files. Full ShellCheck and diff checks pass. Logs are `tmp/native-management-final-native.log`, `tmp/native-management-final-python.log` and `tmp/native-management-final-gates.log`; the private gate session is `tmp/native-management-final-gates-evidence/session.Zydu01/`. Existing narrow GtkText and PyGObject warnings remain recorded. No hosted or paid CI is used.

Substantial review separates unchanged production code, Make/runner tooling (+16/−11), tests/support (+447/−221, including the deleted Python helper), the independent management JSON (5,616 lines/186,074 bytes) and the three added Live focus-cycle observations. Documentation is separate. The new 386-line observer shares the existing assembled owner rather than introducing another application scaffold or test-only production API.

The environment uses private X11/Openbox, GTK 4.22.4, Pango 1.58.2, Libadwaita 1.9.3, scale 1, disabled animations/cursor blinking and software Mesa. HOME/XDG, clipboard, buses, network/PID/mount namespaces are isolated; physical devices and the system bus are masked. No host input, credentials, microphone, user content or installed files are used. The installed app/widget remain v1.6.0; the authorized three-model lineup and default Qwen3-ASR 1.7B are unchanged. Complete joined workflows, page-driven provisioning, remaining Python/tooling removal, clean distribution, platform/device checks and current performance acceptance remain open. Every whole-workflow matrix row stays Pending.
